intro.text: An ancient Veden king who held the throne for only three months.

items.text: No accounts from NanKhet's own time survive. His story was written two hundred years after his death by Natata Ved, known as Oileyes, whose dramatic version reads more like a parable than history.

According to Oileyes, NanKhet inherited the throne from his brother NanHar and survived six assassination attempts in three months, by his sister, her son, a cousin who blinded him in one eye, another brother, an uncle and his own son. Fed up, he had his whole household killed at a feast and cooked his dinner on their pyre, then choked while eating alone, with no one left to help.
The Siln dynasty was founded after his death. Jasnah Kholin finds his story interesting as an example of how common family infighting was in the Vorin kingdoms.
